method.partialPeriodPolicy: October 2026 was excluded because the export was retrieved during that month and its last weekly observation began on the retrieval date.
method.monthlyAggregation: Unweighted arithmetic mean of non-missing weekly Google Trends observations whose start dates fall within each month.
method.demandMeasure: Mean monthly Google Trends interest over the 12 common complete months.
method.supplyMeasure: Mapped category listings divided by all 8 mapped public Chamber-directory listings with coordinates inside the township boundary.
method.gapFormula: z(demand across the five-category comparison cohort) minus z(supply share across the same cohort)

limitations: Google Trends values are relative search-interest indexes, not search volumes, people, customers, or market size.
New Jersey search behavior is broader than Mount Olive and is used only as a regional context signal.
The public Chamber directory is a selected membership directory, not a census of Mount Olive businesses.
Zero mapped listings means no listings in the mapped Chamber sample; it does not mean no local businesses exist.
Only 8 of 40 boundary-matched listings map to this taxonomy, so supply shares are highly sensitive to classification and directory coverage.
The broad term home improvement may include television-program, tax-credit, grant, and do-it-yourself intent unrelated to hiring a local provider.
The broad term childcare may include tax-credit and policy intent unrelated to finding a local provider.
The five terms have different semantic breadth. Their shared scale permits comparison but does not make them equally specific measures of purchase intent.
The result is descriptive and does not establish unmet demand, business viability, market saturation, or causality.
